title: Doesnt Get Along With Others
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses team members whose difficulty forging peer relationships damages team dynamics, arguing leaders should coach specific behaviors rather than diagnose personality. The author lays out a sequence: first gauge the team member's own awareness of the problem through open questions, then reset behavioral expectations for what being a 'good teammate' looks like, and finally assign a specific replacement behavior tailored to what's actually driving the friction. The piece closes on the idea that personalities don't clash -- behaviors do -- and that small behavioral substitutions can resolve outsized relationship problems.
points: Good leaders coach the specific behaviors producing the friction rather than trying to diagnose or relabel a team member's personality.
The process starts by asking, not telling, the team member how aware they are of how others experience them.
A concrete example: someone who talks over others might be asked to wait two to three seconds after others stop speaking before jumping in.
Talking to the rest of the team about why they've pulled away informs the leader's theory of what specific behavior to target.
quotes: Good leaders don’t get caught up in diagnosing the personality of the troubled team member. They focus on the behaviors that produce the problem and help the team member eliminate or correct them.
Questions like “How do your teammates react to you?” and “What’s your read on how team meetings are going?” are conversation starters.
The most essential move is for the leader to ask them to repeatedly enact a specific behavior — depending on what has been derailing their connection to others.
Personalities don’t clash. Behaviors do. By replacing or introducing new behaviors, leaders can coach the troubled team member to greater acceptance and success.
The best leaders don’t coach attitude. They coach actions that others can see and feel. Sometimes, small behavior shifts can fix big relationship problems.
